title: A fixed screen at 2 stellar radii per day fits three G4466 dips if the bare-star flux is 1.285 in the tested model
abstract: We test how an unknown bare-star flux affects screen-speed inferences for the dusty dwarf G4466. A convex linear program finds the smallest bare-star flux for a fixed opacity map that fits 357 TESS measurements across three 2022 dips. At 2 stellar radii per day, a 0.04-radius cell grid gives a bare-star flux of 1.28468 in source units. The brightest observed point is 17.6 percent below this level. A finer integration of the same map gives RMS residual 0.00755, against the source reference error of 0.0064, and maximum residual 0.01294. This extends a prior 4.75-speed map test. Conditional circular orbit examples at the tested speed have radii of 2.03 to 9.73 au for the source mass-radius choices. These dips alone therefore do not exclude several-au orbits when persistent extinction and a flexible screen are allowed. We map the flux-speed tradeoff at five speeds and two deterministic residual tolerances. These tolerances are not confidence levels. The frontier changes with grid size; we claim no continuum lower flux bound, true speed, physical map, or measured dust location. Many free cells, unknown bare-star flux, inherited dilution and correlated noise limit the result. Code, saved maps, source hashes, integration checks, aggregate tables and reproduction instructions are included.

citations.reason: Source photometry, stellar assumptions and rectangular-screen speed limits. The new conditional slow-screen example tests a broader interpretation of those limits.
Direct prior opacity-map existence test at speed 4.75. We extend it to speed 2 and a numerical bare-star-flux versus speed frontier.
